subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a load-time repair that removes dead-end same-parent compaction retry entries from persisted session JSONL, or require write-side retry prevention before repairing existing files?
rationale: The proposed fix changes persisted session state by deleting structurally valid entries that are inferred to be superseded, so maintainer policy is needed before this issue can close.

options.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh
options.body: Refresh or replace the linked PR on current main and land a compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage.

options.title: Require write-side prevention first
options.body: Pause the repair until compaction retry writes are made idempotent or prevented from creating duplicate same-parent compaction entries.

options.title: Split repair and prevention
options.body: Land a narrow existing-file repair now and track write-side duplicate prevention as follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the linked PR on current main and land a compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent validated transcript cache work is the current repair path the candidate fix must fit before the policy can land safely.
